doc.title: Sonny Igoe interviewed by Monk Rowe, Emerson, New Jersey, July 31, 2003

title: Road with B bands before Benny Goodman
summary: Igoe recalls Tommy Reed, Les Elgart and Ina Ray Hutton bands at $90 a week, and hears Goodman is auditioning drummers.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: always had a reputation for paying their guys well. But you worked hard. And it was a very pleasant atmosphere, no problem. And you know I can remember when I started with Benny Goodman’s band, now we’re talking 19 — what would that be, — 19—

’48 and ’49. That’s right. I was going to say ’47. No ’48. And there’s a long story concerned with this, and it’s the thing I told you before. You can’t do anything alone. Somebody’s got to help you. So I had come off the road playing with three what we would call back in those days B bands. They weren’t like the Benny Goodman or that sort of thing. They were like a guy named Tommy Reed who had a band that was made up of all ex-servicemen. I went out to San Francisco to play with him. And then I was with Les Elgart’s band at the Meadowbrook, and then I was with a lady bandleader named Ina Ray Hutton, I don’t know if you ever heard of her. She used to have a girl band but now she had a guy band. And then all those jobs fizzled out and then from one to another you get a call, “would you like to audition for Ina Ray Hutton?” Sure, because I don’t have a gig. And I wasn’t married yet or anything like that. So those bands, Tommy Reed, Ina Ray Hutton and Les Elgart were 90 dollar bands. That’s a week on the road with hotels and meals you had to pay your own.
You had to pay your own.
